Create a function to derive output file paths from a path format

Source: R/pathFormat.R
pathFormat.Rd

Generates a function that constructs file paths according to a path format (a template with placeholders). This is particularly useful in modeling workflows where outputs need to be organized by model name, with consistent naming conventions across files.

Usage

pathFormat(
  path.format = "%name",
  dir,
  model = NULL,
  script = NULL,
  path.funs = NULL,
  structure
)

Arguments

path.format

A character string specifying a path format template, or a custom function. If a function is provided, it is returned without modification.

Templates are specified using %model, %script, and %name placeholders, separated by / to indicate directory levels. The last /-separated component is treated as the file name pattern; any earlier components are directory names. %model is replaced by the model name (with any file extension stripped), %script by the script name (with any file extension stripped), and %name by name (also with its extension stripped, re-attached at the end). Any other characters (e.g. -, _) are kept as literal separators. Examples:

"%model/%name_%model"

Creates paths like model_name/file_model_name.ext. Example: "run001/gof_run001.png".

"%name_%model"

Creates paths like file_model_name.ext with no model subdirectory. Example: "gof_run001.png"

"%model/%model-%name"

Creates paths like model_name/model_name-file.ext. Example: "run001/run001-gof.png"

"%model-%name"

Creates paths like model_name-file.ext with no model subdirectory. Example: "run001-gof.png"

"%script/%name_%model"

Creates paths like script_name/file_model_name.ext. Example: "myscript/gof_run001.png"

Any other combination of %model, %script, %name, literal text, and / is supported - e.g. "archive/%model/plots/%name". Default is "%name", i.e. name is used as is (relative to dir).

dir

Character string specifying the base directory for all outputs. This is prepended to all generated paths. Default is NULL (current directory).

model

Default value for the model argument of the generated function. Used whenever the generated function is called without explicitly supplying model. Default is NULL.

script

Default value for the script argument of the generated function. Used whenever the generated function is called without explicitly supplying script. Default is NULL.

path.funs

Optional named list of functions used to preprocess model and/or script before they are substituted into path.format. Supported names are model and script. Each function takes the value as its single argument and returns a character string. Elements not supplied keep the default, which is function(x) fnExtension(basename(x), "") (strip directory and file extension). Note that a supplied function replaces the default entirely, so e.g. extension stripping must be included if still wanted. Example: path.funs = list(script = function(x) substr(basename(x), 1, 4)). Default is NULL.

structure

Deprecated. Use path.format.

Value

A function with signature function(name, model, script, subdir, dir, quiet = FALSE) that generates file paths according to the specified path format. If path.format is already a function, it is returned unchanged.

Details

The returned function accepts the following arguments:

name

The base file name (typically without extension)

model

A model identifier (character string or model object). If a model object (list) is provided, the $mod element is extracted and used as the model name. The file extension is automatically removed from the model name (e.g., "model.lst" becomes "model").

script

A script identifier (character string, typically a script file name). The file extension is automatically removed (e.g., "myscript.R" becomes "myscript").

subdir

Optional subdirectory. Inserted between the directory components of path.format and the file name component.

dir

Base directory. Overrides the dir argument passed to pathFormat.

quiet

If TRUE, suppress messages about ignored model/script arguments. Default FALSE.

The generated function handles missing model/script arguments gracefully - if path.format does not contain %model (or %script), the corresponding argument is optional and ignored (with a message if supplied anyway). If path.format does contain %model (or %script), the corresponding argument is required.

See also

writer for using path formats in writing functions, ggwrite, ftwrite, lwrite for functions that accept fun.path arguments

Examples

# Create a path function (default format)
path_fun <- pathFormat(path.format = "%model/%name_%model")

# Use it to generate paths
path_fun(name = "gof1.png", model = "run001")
#> [1] "run001/gof1_run001.png"
# Returns: "run001/gof1_run001.png"

path_fun(name = "gof1.png", model = "run001", subdir = "diagnostics")
#> [1] "run001/diagnostics/gof1_run001.png"
# Returns: "run001/diagnostics/gof1_run001.png"

# With base directory
path_fun2 <- pathFormat(path.format = "%model/%model-%name", dir = "outputs")
path_fun2(name = "gof1.png", model = "run001")
#> [1] "outputs/run001/run001-gof1.png"
# Returns: "outputs/run001/run001-gof1.png"

# Different format
path_fun3 <- pathFormat(path.format = "%model-%name")
path_fun3(name = "gof1.png", model = "run001")
#> [1] "run001-gof1.png"
# Returns: "run001-gof1.png"

# Fully custom format
path_fun3b <- pathFormat(path.format = "archive/%model/plots/%name")
path_fun3b(name = "gof1.png", model = "run001")
#> [1] "archive/run001/plots/gof1.png"
# Returns: "archive/run001/plots/gof1.png"

# Format based on script name
path_fun3c <- pathFormat(path.format = "%script/%name_%model")
path_fun3c(name = "gof1.png", model = "run001", script = "myscript")
#> [1] "myscript/gof1_run001.png"
# Returns: "myscript/gof1_run001.png"

# Supplying default model/script to pathFormat() itself
path_fun3d <- pathFormat(path.format = "%script/%name_%model",
                         model = "run001", script = "myscript")
path_fun3d(name = "gof1.png")
#> [1] "myscript/gof1_run001.png"
# Returns: "myscript/gof1_run001.png"

# Explicit arguments to the generated function override the defaults
path_fun3d(name = "gof1.png", model = "run002")
#> [1] "myscript/gof1_run002.png"
# Returns: "myscript/gof1_run002.png"

# Custom preprocessing of script (and/or model) via path.funs
path_fun3e <- pathFormat(path.format = "%script/%name_%model",
                         path.funs = list(script = function(x) substr(basename(x), 1, 4)))
path_fun3e(name = "gof1.png", model = "run001", script = "myscript.R")
#> [1] "mysc/gof1_run001.png"
# Returns: "mysc/gof1_run001.png"

# Custom function (passed through unchanged)
my_fun <- function(name, model, subdir) {
  paste0("custom/", model, "/", name)
}
path_fun4 <- pathFormat(path.format = my_fun)
identical(path_fun4, my_fun)  # TRUE
#> [1] TRUE
